notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). The card's entry class avisengine:Car is confirmed at avisengine.py:17. The package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null): reviewed_by is not claimed, no human tested it, and nothing ran on hardware or on the external AVIS Engine simulator. The device is declared simulated R1; the upstream is a TCP client of the separately downloaded Unity simulator at the documented 127.0.0.1:25001 (README.md:62-63, config.py:5-6), and only the package's own fake backend (.fake:FakeCar) is offered, so no network, socket or hardware path is used. The fake never imports or runs the clone; it implements only Car members (setSpeed, setSteering, setSensorAngle, getData, getSensors, getSpeed, updateData, stop) and its numbers are placeholders (1500 cm sensor readings, sensor angle 30 deg, speed following the throttle), not facts or limits. The external simulator was not contacted, installed, imported or compared with the fake. NOT COVERED: the camera image array returned by Car.getImage (avisengine.py:154-160 decodes it and :179-183 returns it); MHS 0.9 carries no image array field, and the scalar telemetry and controls are served instead. Units: throttle is the dimensionless -100..100 command scale (README.md:132; the clone states no physical unit), steering is degrees (README.md:133, example.py:33), sensor distances are cm (README.md:102, :137) and the current speed is km/h (README.md:107, :139). The throttle and steering Limits cite the README lines and are -100..100; sensor_angle is Limit.operator_required because the clone states no range (example.py:36 only passes 45 degrees). site-limits.example.json is an example operator overlay (0..90 deg), not a statement about a device; every deployment must supply its own bound. The stop action accepts the catalogue's optional deceleration input but the upstream Car.stop takes no deceleration argument (avisengine.py:206-214); only the catalogue schema's minimum applies to it, and no driver Limit is invented. The README claims MIT (README.md:210) but the clone tracks no LICENSE file, so the lock keeps the card's NOASSERTION; this needs a maintainer's licence decision. No x-cap extensions were used, so there are no catalogue requests. The gate printed no warnings; gate.digest is the digest line of the last gate run, and check-report.json is regenerated by every run.
